title: The Price of Fate
next_chapter_hook: Just as Chen Ji fell into deep contemplation, the turtle shell covered with cracks suddenly burst forth with blinding white light, and an elderly yet familiar voice came across time and space—the last testament that Chen Tianming left for his son.

text.content: The Pavilion Master slowly took out a turtle shell from his sleeve, its surface covered with cracks, emanating exactly the same ancient aura as the prop in Chapter Two. Chen Ji's pupils contracted sharply—the pattern of the cracks, the dim luster, were clearly from the same artifact forcibly broken into two halves. The first half is here, but where is the second half...?

dialogue.content: The Pavilion Master gently placed the turtle shell on the table, his voice hoarse like dry leaves rubbing together: "This is the life vessel of the fate writers through the ages—it records the price of each glimpse of heavenly secrets. The first writer Li Qingyun gazed upon heaven seventy-two times, ultimately losing both eyes and dying in madness."

text.content: The candle flames in the Elder Hall flickered, and a illusory figure emerged behind the Pavilion Master—an emaciated old man with sunken eyes like two black holes, yet a strange smile remained at the corners of his mouth, as if mocking the absurdity of fate until death. Chen Ji felt a chill of revulsion rise from his spine.

dialogue.content: "The second writer Zhou Wuya, after gazing upon heaven thirty-one times, gradually lost his sanity, and before his death erased his own name from the world entirely, even his bones turning to nothing." The Pavilion Master paused, his gaze falling on Chen Ji's face, "The third generation... you should have already encountered."

text.content: Chen Ji's breath caught. Mo Xiansheng's face, sometimes lucid and sometimes chaotic, floated through his mind—so it wasn't simply a state of remnant soul, but the traces left by heaven's backlash against the soul after each glimpse of heavenly secrets. He remembered the occasional dazed look in Mo Xiansheng's eyes, and a sense of indescribable sorrow welled up in his heart.

dialogue.content: "The fourth generation..." The Pavilion Master's voice suddenly dropped, and a complex light flickered in those turbid old eyes, "His name was Chen Tianming. He is your father." The Pavilion Master pushed the turtle shell toward Chen Ji, "And the only fate writer who attempted to resist the will of heaven."

text.content: Chen Ji felt his heart being violently gripped by an invisible hand. Father... that figure long blurred in his memory, that man who "died violently" in the deep mountains when he was young—was he actually a fate writer? He stared intently at that turtle shell, his mind in chaos.

dialogue.content: "He gazed upon heaven forty-nine times, the closest among all the writers to 'complete heavenly secrets'." The Pavilion Master's voice seemed to come from far away, "However, the Eye of Heaven does not permit anyone to touch the truth. Your father discovered the true purpose of the Tianji Record—not prophecy, but..."

text.content: The Pavilion Master suddenly stopped, as if weighing whether to continue. After a long while, he slowly spoke: "Reboot." These two words fell into the silent hall, like a boulder thrown into still water, stirring up layers of ripples. Chen Ji's pupils dilated sharply—reboot? Reboot what?

dialogue.content: "The Eye of Heaven does not wish to rule this world." The Pavilion Master's voice carried a trace of sarcastic laughter, "What it wants is to reset everything. To reshape a new world it can completely control. And the Tianji Record... is merely a tool it uses to select its chess pieces."

text.content: Chen Ji suddenly remembered the blurry prophetic images on the Tianji Record Fragment, and the虚脱感 that followed each use. He had always thought it was merely the consumption of "Heavenly Fate Value," never considering... He looked up at the Pavilion Master, his voice somewhat hoarse: "Why did my father resist?"

dialogue.content: The Pavilion Master was silent for a moment, then suddenly asked an seemingly unrelated question: "Do you remember your sister's name?" Chen Ji trembled all over. Chen Nian... his sister who had been missing for years, the sister taken by the Holy Sect as the "Heavenly Fate Key." The Pavilion Master continued: "Because your father discovered the truth, the Eye of Heaven descended the 'Key'... as punishment."

text.content: Chen Ji's fist clenched tightly, his knuckles turning white. All the clues were frantically connecting in his mind—his father's "violent death," his sister's disappearance, the Tianji Record Fragment he accidentally obtained... was all this actually the layout of the Eye of Heaven? His loved ones were merely chess pieces being manipulated between its fingers?

dialogue.content: "Accept the inheritance, and you will obtain the complete Tianji Record, with the ability to gaze upon more distant futures." The Pavilion Master's voice was terrifyingly calm, "The price is—you will ultimately lose yourself, becoming the next puppet devoured by heaven. Refuse..." He glanced meaningfully at Chen Ji, "That sister of yours will likely never be saved."

choice.prompt: The choice of fate lies before Chen Ji, how should he cope with this inescapable selection?

choices.description: For his sister, for uncovering the truth, Chen Ji decided to accept the complete inheritance of the fate writer, even if the road ahead is a bottomless abyss.
choices.risk_hint: All Previous Writers Met Tragic Ends

text.content: Chen Ji took a deep breath, slowly extending his hand, his fingertips touching the cracks on the turtle shell's surface. An icy, piercing force surged into his body through his fingers, and he felt something awakening in his mind—that was the inheritance dormant deep in his bloodline, resonating with his soul.

dialogue.content: "I accept." Chen Ji's voice was low and firm, "But I will not become anyone's chess piece—including heaven."

choices.description: Chen Ji refused to repeat his father's fate. He would rather abandon this power than lose his own clarity, choosing to fight against destiny in his own way.
choices.visible_cost: Losing the chance for further awakening of the Tianji Record

text.content: Chen Ji withdrew his hand, his gaze icy as he stared at the Pavilion Master: 'My father chose to resist, yet you want me to accept the same fate? Sorry, but I, Chen Ji, will never be a piece moved by others.'

dialogue.content: 'I will have my own path.' A cold smile curved Chen Ji's lips, 'a path even the Eyes of Heavenly Dao cannot foresee.'

choices.description: Chen Ji refused to accept or to abandon. He decided to use all existing information to carve out a different route, finding a new path to break the Heavenly Dao's布局.
choices.visible_cost: Extremely high risk, possibility of success unknown
choices.visible_reward: Possibly finding the true method to break the situation
choices.risk_hint: Possibly incurring the wrath of both the Eyes of Heavenly Dao and the Pavilion of Heavenly Secrets

text.content: Chen Ji suddenly burst into laughter. That smile carried a hint of madness, a touch of relief. He thought of the chess game his father left behind, of Mo Xiansheng's words that stopped just short of speaking, of his sister's blurry prophetic visions—perhaps the answer was never within the inheritance.

dialogue.content: 'All of you are telling me what to do—accept or refuse, obey or resist.' Chen Ji raised his head, his eyes blazing with dangerous light, 'But have any of you considered... that I could flip the entire chessboard?'

text.content: Just then, the turtle shell quietly resting on the table suddenly burst forth with blinding white light. The cracks writhed like living creatures, and an ancient, familiar aura gushed forth from within. The Pavilion Master's face changed dramatically: 'This is... impossible! How could he have left a remnant consciousness in the Life Coffin!'

dialogue.content: Within the white light, a vague human silhouette slowly coalesced. It was the outline of a middle-aged man, his features bearing a seventy percent resemblance to Chen Ji, though his brow carried more hardship and defiance. He looked at Chen Ji, his lips moving, his voice seeming to traverse endless years: 'Ji'er... it's your father.'

text.content: Chen Ji froze, his throat feeling blocked by something. He wanted to call out 'Father,' but found his voice choking in his throat, unable to emerge. That figure, already vague in memory, now appeared so vividly before his eyes, carrying a warmth he had never experienced.

dialogue.content: Chen Tianming's phantom stretched out an illusory hand, brushing across Chen Ji's cheek—the touch was like a spring breeze, yet carried a faint chill. 'Father was incompetent, unable to protect you.' His voice was laden with infinite guilt, 'But there is something you must know—Nian'er... she was not taken by the Holy Sect.'

text.content: Chen Ji's pupils dilated sharply, waves of shock crashing in his heart. His sister wasn't taken by the Holy Sect? Then where did she go? He stared fixedly at his father's phantom, waiting for an answer that might overturn all his understanding.

dialogue.content: 'She was... I sent her away myself.' Chen Tianming's phantom trembled violently, as if maintaining this form had exhausted his final strength, 'To protect her, to let her become... a variable to break the Heavenly Dao. Ji'er, find her. Only when you siblings unite can you...' Before he could finish, the phantom began to fade.

text.content: 'Father!' Chen Ji lunged to grab, but only touched emptiness. The white light gradually faded, and another crack appeared on the turtle shell, as if it had borne too much undeserved karma. The Pavilion Master watched this scene, his murky old eyes flickering with complex light, but he said nothing.

Chen Ji knelt in place, long silent. His father's dying words were like a thunderclap, shattering what he thought was correct understanding. His sister wasn't a victim, but... another piece his father had positioned? And what about himself? Was obtaining the Tianji Record Fragment coincidence, or a fate already planned?

dialogue.content: 'It seems your father left you a 'surprise'.' The Pavilion Master's voice broke the silence as he settled back into his chair, his tone regaining that chilling calm, 'But this also proves—the inheritance was never truly severed. Before your father perished, he sealed his final remnant consciousness into the Life Coffin, waiting for this moment.'

text.content: Chen Ji slowly stood up, his expression terrifyingly calm. He gazed at the cracked turtle shell, then at the Pavilion Master, a cold smile forming at the corner of his mouth: 'It seems what my father left me is not only a remnant consciousness.' He paused, his eyes flashing, 'But also a path... none of you could have anticipated.'

The Pavilion Master's gaze shifted slightly, as if reevaluating this 'waste' disciple. Chen Ji had already turned toward the door, his back resolute. 'Wait.' The Pavilion Master's voice came from behind, 'Have you thought this through? How will you proceed from here?' Chen Ji did not look back, leaving only words floating in the wind:

'Find her first.' Chen Ji's voice was soft, yet carried unwavering resolve, 'I will find Chen Nian, then personally overturn this chess game.' The words fell, and his figure vanished at the doorway of the Elders' Hall. Behind him, the Pavilion Master gazed at his departing direction, a meaningful smile actually curling at his lips—as if Chen Ji's choice was precisely the answer he had long awaited.
